dimensions.label: Income consistency
dimensions.about: How steady your income is from month to month. Swing means how far a typical month is from your average month. A full score needs a swing of 15% or less; the score is zero at 100% or more.
dimensions.measure: Your monthly income swung 173% around its average of USD 375 over 12 months.
dimensions.needed: To score higher, make your months more even. At a swing of 15% or less you get all 25 points; yours is 173%.
steps: No payment is recorded in 9 of your 12 full months. If you were paid in any of them, record the payment; until you do, they count as months with no income.

dimensions.label: Profit margin
dimensions.about: How much of what you earn is left after the business expenses you recorded. A full score needs 60% or more left; the score is zero at 0% or less. Only expenses recorded in LanceraOS count. Personal spending and savings are not tracked here.
dimensions.measure: Your expenses were as high as or higher than your income: USD 4,500 received, USD 8,400 spent.
dimensions.needed: To score higher, keep more of your income. When 60% or more is left you get all 20 points; you kept nothing.

dimensions.label: Tax compliance
dimensions.about: Whether your tax basics are in place: an NTN saved (8 points), PSEB registration marked (4 points), a payment recorded in the last 90 days (4 points) and an expense recorded in the last 90 days (4 points). The NTN and PSEB are what you entered; LanceraOS does not check them with FBR or PSEB. PSEB registration is for people who export IT services, so it may not apply to your work.
dimensions.needed: To score higher, complete the missing checks: NTN saved; Payment recorded in the last 90 days; Expense recorded in the last 90 days.
steps: Save your NTN in Settings, then Tax & PSEB. An NTN is the number you need to file a tax return with FBR. This is worth about 8 points of your score.
No payment is recorded in the last 90 days. Record the money you have received on the Payments page. This is worth about 4 points of your score.
No expense is recorded in the last 90 days. Record your business costs on the Expenses page, so your profit is not overstated. This is worth about 4 points of your score.

dimensions.label: Income growth
dimensions.about: How your average month compares with your average month in the same number of months before it. A full score needs growth of 30% or more, flat income earns half the points, and a fall of 30% or more scores zero.
dimensions.measure: Your average month was USD 375 over the last 12 months, against USD 900 over the 6 months before (down 58%).
dimensions.needed: To score higher, grow your average month. At growth of 30% or more you get all 20 points; yours is down 58%.
steps: Your average month was USD 375 over the last 12 months, against USD 900 over the 6 months before. An average month of USD 990 (10% above the earlier months) would raise this area. This is worth about 13 points of your score.

dimensions.label: Client diversity
dimensions.about: How much of your income depends on one payer, using the "Received from" name on your payments. A full score needs your biggest payer to be 30% or less of your named income; the score is zero at 80% or more. This needs a name on at least 70% of your income.
dimensions.measure: Solo Client paid 100% of the income that has a name (USD 4,500 of USD 4,500). You have 1 named payer.
dimensions.needed: To score higher, spread your income across more payers. When your biggest payer is 30% or less you get all 15 points; yours is 100%.
steps: Solo Client paid 100% of the income that has a name (USD 4,500 of USD 4,500). If your biggest payer were 50% of it, that would raise this area. This is worth about 9 points of your score.
